reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that nanolayered structures in a high-entropy alloy-based glass suppress shear banding and cause strain delocalization during nanoindentation, directly supporting the barrier and delocalization premises. However, it does not address time-dependent deformation (creep) or sustained loading, leaving the link to creep resistance unsupported.
premises: Nanolayered structures suppress shear banding in metallic glasses
Interfaces act as barriers to shear band propagation
Suppressed shear banding leads to strain delocalization
